title: Nikita Kucherov trade request: 5 potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP - CBS Sports
description: Kucherov's days with the Lightning appear to be over
body:
Kucherov's days with the Lightning appear to be over
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.
It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Montreal CanadiensRight out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota WildWe already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need. However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Carolina HurricanesIt was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Utah MammothSimilar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.
Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dallas StarsAllow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

title: Who is Christian Mbilli? Get to know the fighter ready to face Canelo Alvarez - CBS Sports
description: The 31-year-old carries knockout power and his size could pose a problem for Alvarez
body:
The 31-year-old carries knockout power and his size could pose a problem for Alvarez
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        On Saturday, Christian Mbilli will receive the biggest opportunity of his career when he steps in the ring to defend his WBC super middleweight championship against Saul "Canelo" Alvarez. While Mbilli has yet to taste defeat as a professional, the oddsmakers are favoring Alvarez, who has firmly cemented himself as a first-ballot Hall of Famer.Mbilli was the beneficiary of Alvarez's most recent fight, a loss to Terence Crawford in September 2025. After Crawford's decision to retire following a career-best victory, Mbilli was elevated from interim to full champion.Mbilli won the interim belt two fights ago, knocking out Maciej Sulecki in the first round of their June 2025 meeting. In his final fight before being elevated to full champion, Mbilli battled to a hard-fought split draw against Lester Martinez.What are Mbilli's strengths?Mbilli is a bruiser with a high-pressure style. He's muscular and strong and that allows him to bully many fighters. Of his 29 career victories, 24 have come via knockout, which speaks to his ability to turn his pressure into finishing power.
Mbilli's forward style benefits when he can back opponents toward the ropes. With an opponent trapped, Mbilli will look to throw thudding right hands to the head while also keeping a focus on throwing nasty left hands to the body, which can break opponents down if Mbilli's power doesn't catch them with a knockout shot up top.It took just 40 seconds for Mbilli to finish Mark Heffron with a body shot in their fight.Mbilli also benefits from a willingness to dirty it up in the ring. There are very few comfortable moments when Mbilli is on his game.
What are Mbilli's weaknesses?The downside to Mbilli's style is twofold, and both were on display in his draw with Martinez, a fight where he'd built up a strong early lead.Mbilli throws a lot of punches (78 per round over his five most recent fights), and a lot of them are power shots (58 per round). The power output is twice the super middleweight average, but it can lead to Mbilli fatiguing as the fight wears on. He carries a lot of muscle, which combines with his high-output style to put a lot of stress on his body, and that showed in a 10-round fight with Martinez.Mbilli also leaves himself open to counters in pursuit of big power punches. Those openings become even bigger as Mbilli fatigues.
Even when fighting with effectively one arm after suffering an injury early in the fight, Sergiy Derevyanchenko was able to find some big counters through the mid and late rounds against Mbilli.
How can Mbilli defeat Alvarez?The oddsmakers have Mbilli a +250 underdog heading into Saturday, which is certainly closer than the fight would have been seen even a year or two ago.Alvarez has gone eight fights without scoring a stoppage, which is something of a red flag for an aging fighter whose power had previously been a key factor in his fights. He does have enough pop to hurt any fighter if he lands clean, and as noted, Mbilli leaves openings for opponents to land heavy counters.
Still, the path to victory for Mbilli is fairly clear. He's a bigger man than Alvarez and thrives when he can be the bully in the ring. Alvarez isn't a high-output offensive fighter, so Mbilli has the chance to force Alvarez into an uncomfortable brawl, pushing the pace and trying to outwork his more technically gifted opponent.As Terence Crawford told DAZN, "Styles make fights, and Mbilli's style is tailor-made for Canelo. Mbilli can't do nothing but press Canelo. I don't see him beating Canelo in a boxing match. I think his best success will be letting his hands go, roughing Canelo up, and making it a dogfight."Who wins Alvarez vs. Mbilli, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $2,500 on his combat sports picks last year, and find out.

title: LOOK: Cardinals' Budda Baker addresses trade rumors while wearing Halloween costume - CBS Sports
description: Baker isn't letting trade speculation spoil his Halloween spirit
body:
Baker isn't letting trade speculation spoil his Halloween spirit
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For several years, Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker has worn a costume to practice around Halloween. Baker continued the tradition on Friday and quickly went viral after fielding questions about his future with the Cardinals while wearing his costume. It's easy to see why the moment quickly went viral. While Baker gave a standard answer, his appearance while addressing a relatively serious matter was funny ... even if you're a Cardinals fan. "I just live in the present," Baker responded. "You know, look like today, having a great time with you guys, and gonna have a great Friday practice and just focus on playing against the Dallas Cowboys and trying to get a W at their stadium." 
Costume aside, Baker's future with the Cardinals is no laughing matter. While the Cardinals would potentially get sizable assets in a trade involving him, it's safe to say that a large portion of Arizona fans would be sad to see him go given his status as one of the greatest players in franchise history. 
A lifetime Cardinal, Baker is in the middle of his 10th season in Arizona. He's an eight-time Pro Bowler and has been named to the Pro Bowl each of the last seven years. Baker is also a two-time All-Pro. Unfortunately for Cardinals/Baker fans, the NFL is a business, and teams in the midst of a bad season (Arizona is 2-5) often trade talented veterans before the trade deadline in exchange for future draft picks. If the Cardinals trade Baker this season, they have until now and November 10 at 4 p.m. ET. There is, however, a chance that the Cardinals don't trade Baker before the deadline. This isn't the first time that there have been rumblings about his future with the team; he reportedly requested a trade in 2023, over a year before he signed a lucrative long-term contract with the team. It would also require a team making Arizona a pretty sweet deal for the 30-year-old Baker. 
For now, Baker is still a Cardinal. And, based on Friday's press conference, he doesn't appear to be terribly worried about his status in Arizona ahead of the trade deadline.

title: Ja Morant injury: Trail Blazers star expected to miss at least four weeks with hamstring strain - CBS Sports
description: Another day, another notable injury in the NBA -- and this time, Morant is expected to miss at least a month
body:
Another day, another notable injury in the NBA -- and this time, Morant is expected to miss at least a month
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Portland Trail Blazers star Ja Morant will miss at least the next four weeks after suffering a Grade 2 left hamstring sprain on Thursday against the Memphis Grizzlies, the team announced. Morant was facing his former team for the first time since being traded earlier this summer and exited with 7:46 remaining in the game and didn't return.Morant missed a floater in the lane and went to grab his own miss when he appeared to suffer the injury. Morant stayed in the game for two more defensive possessions before checking out at the next stoppage of play. In 23 minutes of action, Morant finished with 14 points, three assists and two rebounds.
        
            
                NBA's 'unprecedented' early season injury crisis has players and coaches searching for answers
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The 124-103 loss to the Grizzlies marked Portland's first defeat of the 2026-27 campaign after starting the season with wins over the Lakers, Kings and Suns.Morant played in just 79 total games over the last three seasons before being traded to Portland this offseason, including logging just 20 appearances during the 2025-26 season. In his first four games with Portland, Morant was averaging 15.8 points, 5.5 assists and 2.5 rebounds.
Where does Portland go from here?With Morant set to miss at least the next four weeks, the Blazers will likely start veteran guard Jrue Holiday in his absence. Heading into the season, one of the main storylines and lineup questions in the NBA was who Portland would start in the backcourt. The Trail Blazers entered the season with a self-made logjam at the position with Morant, Damian Lillard, Holiday, and former No. 3 overall pick Scoot Henderson — who is set to be a restricted free agent this summer — all on the roster. The rotation questions didn't even factor in Shaedon Shapre, who is out for the foreseeable future after suffering a torn lateral meniscus in his right knee in late August.
        
            
                Five ways the NBA's injury outbreak could impact trade season: OKC has work to do, Rockets are in control
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
First-year coach Micah Nori has played Lillard the most (29.5 minutes per game) of the bunch, with Morant (25.8), Holiday (25.3) and Henderson (18.8) not far behind. With Morant out, Henderson could slide into a larger role as the first guard off the bench, even though Sidy Cissoko (22.8) is averaging more minutes per game than Henderson.
Portland ranks No. 2 in the NBA (101.3) in defensive rating through the first week and a half of the season. That number should improve even more with Holiday set to enter the starting lineup.Morant is the latest NBA star who will miss timeAn unfortunate trend through the first week and a half of the season has been injuries. Morant is the latest NBA star who is set to miss time.Current NBA stars set to miss the next few games, at minimum — with some set to be out for even longer stretches: Anthony Edwards, Paolo Banchero, Kawhi Leonard, Jaren Jackson Jr., Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams. On top of those injuries, Brandon Ingram, Jimmy Butler, Kon Knueppel and Kristaps Porziņģis are among the players who have yet to make their season debut. 
Ben Simmons, who was expected to play a significant role for the Kings this season, tore his Achilles in practice days before the season opener and will miss the entire 2026-27 season.

title: WNBA Finals Game 7 predictions: Will the Dream or Valkyries win their first title on Saturday? - CBS Sports
description: It's the first Game 7 in WNBA history on Saturday night in San Francisco ... so who will capture the crown?
body:
It's the first Game 7 in WNBA history on Saturday night in San Francisco ... so who will capture the crown?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It all comes down to Saturday in the 2026 WNBA Finals. It's Game 7 for the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream, and one franchise will win its first championship on Saturday night.The Dream forced this winner-take-all game -- the first Game 7 in WNBA history -- on Thursday. In a matinee at State Farm Arena, the Dream jumped out to a 25-point lead in the first half and held on for an 11-point win. Can Angel Reese and Atlanta finish the job on Saturday? Or will the Valkyries, Gabby Williams and a raucous home crowd propel Golden State to the title? We're making our picks below.WNBA Finals Game 7 picks
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Lindsay Gibbs
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Jack Maloney
                            
            Valkyries vs. Dream
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Dream
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Valkyries
                    
    
    Gibbs: It feels fitting that this historic 30th WNBA season, that began with a hard-fought CBA that elevated player compensation into a new echelon, is ending in the league's first-ever Game 7.
But let's face it: This has not been a series of beautiful basketball. The Valkyries are shooting 34.5% from the field and 26.4% from 3 in the Finals, while the Dream are faring only marginally better, averaging 37.2% and 28.5%, respectively. However, it has been an incredibly compelling showcase of defense and mental fortitude, two aspects of the game that often get the short shrift. Both teams have had to pull themselves off the mat after punches that were potential knockouts; both teams have gained momentum just to have it halted; both teams have relied on their unity and self belief and confidence and grit to make it to this final do-or-die game.And now that we're here, it truly does feel like a toss-up. While the Dream's sensational first quarter on Thursday made the Game 7 possible, the way the Valkyries kept fighting in the game — winning the second half by nine points and whittling down a 25-point Dream lead to nine with just over a minute to play — set that Game 7 up to be a true prize fight. I keep thinking about what Veronica Burton said in the press conference after the Valkyries lost Game 6 in Atlanta by a score of 80-69."My body language is bad. But at the end of the day, we feel good. Yes, we lost. It was a bad game for us. We had a terrible first quarter. We cleaned it up. We found a way. We didn't quit," Burton said. "Games ... 2 and 3 were ugly. We quit. We looked bad, and we didn't quit on this one."The Valkyries were unable to match the Dream's sense of urgency in Game 6, but on Saturday, both teams will be facing elimination. Urgency should permeate every pass, every possession, every heart palpitation. Given the Valkyries are playing in front of their home crowd at Ballhalla, it is tempting to give them the edge.And yet, I'm still backing Atlanta. Earlier in this series, it was Angel Reese alone willing the Dream to wins in Game 2 and 3. But after a lackluster start to the series – and playoffs as a whole, truly – Rhyne Howard has found her stroke and averaged 19 points per game in the last four games of the Finals. And on Thursday, Allisha Gray – who has been playing the series with only eight healthy fingers after an injury in the semifinal series – came alive with 23 points. Essentially, there are three Dream players that I trust more than any Valkyries player to generate offense and make a basket when it matters the most.When we had to make our picks before the series, I picked Dream in 7 and wrote this:"In the spirit of Angel Reese and Joe Lacob, I am manifesting an epic seven-game series full of twists and turns. And, at the end, it will be a big defensive play by Reese that will seal the title for the Dream on the road in front of a raucous Ballhalla crowd on Halloween night."I've been wrong about so many things this postseason, but I'm still feeling good about that one. Dream in 7.Maloney: I picked the Valkyries in six before the series. That, obviously, can no longer happen, but I'm sticking with the Valkyries to win Game 7.The Dream have far more offensive upside, as we've seen at various points throughout this series, including the first quarter of Game 6, when they hit six 3-pointers and scored 32 points en route to a season-saving victory. But the Valkyries are one of the best defensive teams we've ever seen, and have spent much of the series dragging the Dream into the mud for a low-efficiency scrap. We saw that too in Game 6, when the Valkyries held the Dream to 48 points on 16-of-47 shooting (34%) with 15 turnovers.We've never had a Game 7 in the WNBA before, but we've seen the Finals go the distance plenty of times. And the winner-take-all contests to decide the title are often exactly the type of game the Valkyries want to play: slow-paced, low-scoring and extremely physical. In the last five winner-take-all games in the Finals, only one team -- the 2019 Washington Mystics -- has reached 80 points.
Last five winner-take-all games in WNBA Finals2024: Liberty 67, Lynx 622019: Mystics 89, Sun 782017: Lynx 70, Sparks 682016: Sparks 77, Lynx 762015: Lynx 69, Fever 52For whatever reason, be it the weird start time, fatigue or a sense of comfort after going up 3-2, the Valkyries didn't throw the first punch in Game 6, and the action got away from them."This is win or die. This is do or die. This is it," Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said after Game 6. "You want to have that physicality. You want to have that fight. You want to lay it all out there. That's what the Finals is about is just an empty-the-tank mentality, and shoot, we didn't do that [Thursday]."Back in Ballhalla Boohalla, in front of a sold-out crowd on Halloween, the Valkyries will empty the tank in Game 7 and win the first championship in franchise history.

title: Francesco Totti's memorable 2002 volley vs. Udinese remains a Roma masterpiece - CBS Sports
description: The AS Roma captain scored one of the most beautiful goals of his career against Udinese in 2002
body:
The AS Roma captain scored one of the most beautiful goals of his career against Udinese in 2002
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Udinese will host AS Roma on Saturday at the Bluenergy Stadium, a key game that might determine the future of Udinese manager Kosta Runjaic but could also boost the Giallorossi's Scudetto hopes. Gian Piero Gasperini's side is just four points behind league leaders Lazio and Inter. With the Derby della Madonnina set to take place later on Saturday, a victory for Roma would provide a significant boost and allow them to close the gap at the top of the table. The fixture also reminds AS Roma fans of a goal that made history, arguably one of the best scored by the legendary captain Francesco Totti in the Giallorossi jersey. You can watch Saturday's match between Udinese and AS Roma on CBS, and for all the best Serie A action all season long make sure to check out Paramount+.Totti, one of the most recognizable Italian football players in the history of the game, retired in 2017 and left an unforgettable mark at the club, winning the 2000-01 Serie A title, the last one won by the Giallorossi. Totti, who spent his whole career with his childhood club, scored 307 goals in 786 appearances for AS Roma. Some of those are still in the minds of AS Roma fans, such as the one scored against Udinese at the Stadio Olimpico in October 2002. How to watch Udinese vs. RomaDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 1 p.m. ETLocation: Bluenergy Stadium -- Udine, ItalyTV: CBSOdds: Udinese +448; Draw +337; AS Roma -198Speaking to Corriere dello Sport on the goal scored at the Stadio Olimpico on October 2, 2002, Totti said: "For me, one of the best goals, aside from the ones I scored in Genoa, Inter and the derby, was a goal I scored against Udinese at the Stadio Olimpico. I scored twice that day... Batistuta dinks the ball over the goalkeeper, a little chip. I bring the ball under control with my head, I can't remember whether Bertotto was marking me and, with my back to goal, where De Sanctis was, I hit a volley on the half-bounce into the top corner at the far post."

title: CeeDee Lamb says Cowboys have a Cardinals boogeyman: 'They've punched us in the mouth every single time' - CBS Sports
description: Dallas five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb has never beaten Arizona, and they have won eight of the last
body:
Dallas five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb has never beaten Arizona, and they have won eight of the last nine matchups
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys (3-4) have an Arizona Cardinals (2-5) problem they're looking to halt in Week 8. Arizona has won four consecutive games against Dallas as part of a larger span of success that includes wins in eight of the last matchups dating back to 2008. Cowboys five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is in his seventh NFL season in 2026, has never beaten Arizona, losing all four matchups since he was drafted by Dallas in 2020. Why has Dallas struggled so much against the Cardinals? CBS Sports asked Lamb about that and if he has a heightened focus entering the matchup. Lamb's answer? The Cardinals have seemingly wanted it more. "I've never beaten the Cardinals since I've been in the league. So that's fair to say," Lamb said after practice on Thursday. "I wouldn't say [we have a] heightened focus, but it's definitely a note to take. It's just crazy. We've been very relaxed, and they've punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy. "Just coming into the game, they're more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o'clock [1 Eastern], Monday night, Sunday night. We played them in primetime; they beat us there. Just coming in and treating them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be. Hats off to them in their prep. We just have to go match them, if not overpower that."   
Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer disagreed with his top target's assessment, instead pointing to "the ball." The Cowboys have a -11 turnover margin (15 turnovers to four) across the nine matchups since 2008. In Dallas' "Monday Night Football" home loss in Week 9 last season, the Cowboys committed three turnovers and didn't generate a takeaway. Quarterback Dak Prescott had an interception, and both running back Javonte Williams and tight end Jake Ferguson lost fumbles. That put the Cowboys in a 17-point hole minutes into the second half.Arizona's win against Dallas in 2025 was the only victory in 12 starts for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett in 2025.  Schottenheimer has a point. Across all three of the Cowboys' wins this season, they have committed zero turnovers. All four of Dallas' losses in 2026 involve at least one turnover. "I'll disagree with CeeDee a little bit," said Schottenheimer on Friday. "I know why: minus-11 turnover differential in those games. Last year, we were minus-three. So the ball is what this game is going to come down to. I don't think it has to do with energy." 
Cowboys vs. Cardinals, Last 18 yearsResultWeek 9, 2025 (MNF)Cardinals 27, Cowboys 17Week 3, 2023Cardinals 28, Cowboys 16Week 17, 2021Cardinals 25, Cowboys 22Week 6, 2020 (MNF)Cardinals 38, Cowboys 10Week 3, 2017 (MNF)Cowboys 28, Cardinals 17Week 9, 2014Cardinals 28, Cowboys 17Week 13, 2011Cardinals 19, Cowboys 13Week 16, 2010Cardinals 27, Cowboys 26Week 6, 2008Cardinals 30, Cowboys 24Dallas should be able to stop the slide on Sunday as seven-point home favorites, according to DraftKings Sportsbook. The Cardinals enter Week 8 as the NFL's worst scoring defense, allowing 29.7 points per game. Offensively, Arizona enters Week 8 as the league's worst red zone offense, scoring touchdowns on just 42.9% of its red zone drives. Dallas enters Week 8 as the NFL's No. 5 scoring offense (27.0 points per game), with new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. helping calm things down for Dallas' defense. There's only one way for the Cowboys to bury their Cardinals boogeyman narrative: just win. "We got to win," said Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott after practice on Thursday. "They've had our number these last couple of years. Credit to their defense, credit to the way that those guys come in and play and execute. It's a new year. We just have to make sure we go out and take care of business."

An eight-game winless skid and public pushback from leaders like Bruno Fernandes have left Old Trafford fractured ahead of a critical clash with Chelsea

                    at

                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        To the surprise of many, Michael Carrick will continue to be in the dugout for Manchester United as they face Chelsea on Saturday. During their eight-game winless run in all competitions, United have allowed 15 goals while scoring six, and off the pitch, everything is unraveling, with players and fans alike questioning the direction of the club. United have been in this position before, and it has usually led to a change of manager and a rebuild of the club from the ground up.  But what's different is that during this rut, players are publicly speaking out. While things will sometimes leak via undisclosed sources, players saying the quiet part out loud about what's going on with the club is not a good look. Defender Lisandro Martinez spoke about the need for the club to have higher standards and claimed that it's lacking ambition after a poor loss to Atletico Madrid in Champions League play, but it went from bad to worse as captain Bruno Fernandes spoke out after a humbling loss to Como, questioning the team's tactics.How to watch Chelsea vs. Manchester United, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 8:30 a.m. ETLocation: Stamford Bridge  -- LondonTV: USA NetworkOdds: Chelsea -105; Draw +270; Manchester United +270That led to Fernandes being benched and United failing yet again to pick up a victory. While the public view is that Fernandes will retain his captaincy, the episode has to strip away at least some of Carrick's authority within the club.  "There is no decision to be made on [the captaincy]," Carrick said. "It will be Bruno. Listen, we're clear with the situation of the team and as a football club at the moment. He's an important player for this group. He has been and he will be."  Ahead of a match where both teams are struggling, the slightest lack of balance could lead to yet another United loss. With no clear sign that authority lies with the manager rather than the captain, especially after Carrick held meetings about the future of his job, this could get worse before it gets better.  What do you do if United concede an early goal and the match goes off the rails? On the evidence we've seen, it's tough to say Carrick will be able to get the club out of that spiral, and if he can't, there's no reason why he should be the manager. On paper, while too much money was invested in the midfield instead of defense, this isn't a bad squad, but United find themselves in the relegation race only one season after qualifying for Champions League play. Even their numbers scream midtable, not doomed to relegation.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            That's where the mentality of the squad comes in. It's been a persistent issue since Sir Alex Ferguson left, and it's not an issue that seems to be going away anytime soon. At times, it will lie dormant for a season during which you think United are righting the ship, only to come back at the worst time possible. Carrick is only a symptom of a larger issue at Manchester United, and the club has gone through eight permanent managers since Ferguson without sustained success. It's not for lack of spending, and even though there are questions around who is recruited, for the most part, the squads have been fine. They just can never perform to the sum of their parts.
Since Jim Ratcliffe took over, the club has been more focused on profits off the pitch than actual success on it, and that's catching up with United. Turning that around is going to be quite a challenge. Fan protests have been seen, but they aren't igniting real change, and we may be in a situation where United need a sustained spell in the bottom half of the table to lead to anything different. In short, this is already dire, and every day with Carrick at the helm delays the start of that turnaround, even if that isn't his fault. United have become a club without a direction, and that's something Chelsea can take advantage of as the Xabi Alonso era at Stamford Bridge has signs of success but needs a result to get back on the right track.

title: Anthony Colandrea returning to Nebraska in 2027: Huskers QB signs new deal - CBS Sports
description: Matt Rhule and the Huskers retained one of their top players before the start of a busy portal cycle
body:
Matt Rhule and the Huskers retained one of their top players before the start of a busy portal cycle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Nebraska senior quarterback Anthony Colandrea has re-signed with the Huskers for the 2027 season, his agent confirmed to ESPN on Friday. Colandrea, who transferred last offseason from UNLV, has another year of eligibility due to the NCAA's "5-for-5" ruling and has been a much-needed, steady leader for the Huskers, throwing for 1,570 yards, 14 touchdowns and four interceptions to go along with 339 yards on the ground and four scores.This is the first known player contract extension in program history, continuing a trend in college football's new era of talent retention and contracts enabled by NIL and revenue sharing."In today's college football landscape, where the challenges and obstacles seem to multiply by the week, getting a process like this across the finish line as cleanly and seamlessly as we did is no small thing," Colandrea's agent Noah Reisenfeld wrote in a message to CBS Sports. "Pat Stewart, Logan Holgerson, and everyone in that building were nothing short of outstanding to work with through every step of it. Proud to have been a part of something this meaningful for Anthony and the program. Go Big Red."Earlier this month, Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said several SEC programs were already tampering with his quarterback ahead of this fall's transfer portal cycle, which officially begins Jan. 4 and closes nine days later.
"I don't think that's a good narrative for us to have out there that he doesn't have enough support," Rhule said. "I don't think that's good for our players. And not good because he's already got SEC schools calling him. I don't want Nebraska people to start saying that, because that's happened before here. We don't need that now here."Nebraska started the season 5-0 under Rhule before consecutive three-point losses to Indiana and Oregon this month torpedoed the team's shot at spearheading Big Ten championship efforts.The Huskers were on the verge of being ranked behind Colandrea's consistent play before those hiccups in the Big Ten games, during which Nebraska led in the fourth quarter.
"Like I said, I think we're two plays away from being in the big, big conversation," Rhule said entering last week's open date ahead of Saturday's return to the field vs. Washington. But we're not out yet, so we're going to just try to get better this week."Colandrea's impact for Huskers in 2027Colandrea is the second standout this season to re-sign with his current program, joining Oregon State's Jesse Legree, one of the nation's leading wide receivers. Colandrea brought stability to Nebraska's offense after the Huskers watched former five-star Dylan Raiola leave after the 2026 campaign and transfer to Oregon.Entering Week 9, Colandrea and the Huskers rank second in the Big Ten in scoring offense (35.5 points per game), fifth in total offense and third in explosive plays. Colandrea has been an ideal fit in Dana Holgorsen's scheme given his dual-threat ability and wrinkle in a run game that is the most potent of Rhule's tenure at 194.3 yards on the ground per game.
Colandrea said before the season he felt Nebraska's offensive line was the best he had ever played with and trusted that would be one of the strengths of the team. The Huskers allotted a chunk of this season's football share to their offensive front, including the acquisition of former South Carolina tackle "Big" Tree Babalade in the portal.The return of QB1 in 2027 for Rhule is the first piece of the puzzle for a team with College Football Playoff expectations, given the skill talent coming back and the likelihood of the 24-team expanded postseason being beneficial in the Big Ten.

title: What's wrong with Kai Havertz and can he fix it in time for Liverpool vs. Arsenal showdown - CBS Sports
description: Arsenal desperately need a decisive finisher at Anfield, but their versatile striker enters Sunday's massive test
body:
Arsenal desperately need a decisive finisher at Anfield, but their versatile striker enters Sunday's massive test against Liverpool mired in a sharp dip in form and a baffling offside trend
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        If last season's visit to Anfield taught Arsenal anything, it was the need for a killer in the final third to break the game open. Fail to do so and they are vulnerable to the sort of magic that bamboozled them in August of last year, even if the man who scored that brilliant free-kick winner, Dominik Szoboszlai, is a doubt for Liverpool on Sunday.And if this game is indeed one that will be decided by what Mikel Arteta terms the "moments players," then it could scarcely have come at a worse time for the Arsenal manager. Bukayo Saka -- the Gunners' top shot taker, goal scorer and expected goals compiler -- has more than a month left on the sidelines with the thigh injury he suffered in Munich. Noni Madueke could miss the trip with an ankle injury. Christos Tzolis has returned to training but has not played for his new club in more than a month. Max Dowman, the precocious youngster whom Arteta has already entrusted with turning the tide on Merseyside, will serve the first of a three-game ban for his controversial red card.It speaks to the depth at Arteta's disposal that, even if none of the aforementioned quartet play, there will still be game changers in the side. Even so, this does feel like an occasion where a first-choice center forward in top form would be handy. Kai Havertz is not that. Twelve games in and this has been perhaps the weirdest season of all since this esoteric forward landed on English soil in 2020. At his best, he has blown his former club Chelsea away. His worst, meanwhile, includes a wasteful performance in the EFL Cup defeat at Fleetwood and a baffling new tendency to slip offside. 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            The obvious answer when a player slides from peak to trough in a matter of weeks is to consult his injury record. Havertz did return from the last international break early after straining a muscle and went straight back into the side, playing an hour against Leeds and featuring in every other game since. In those six games he has no goals and one assist. In most of the minutes he has played, he has struggled to link the Arsenal attack together the way he usually does, let alone to threaten the opposition goal. That is not, however, a hangover from his injury travails.
"There's nothing to do with that," said Arteta. "It's true that in terms of the numbers, we have dropped those numbers but he certainly had the chances as well to play."That was the case against Fleetwood, seven shots for the German adding up to 0.72 expected goals. That sounds perfectly adequate on first pass, and there are certainly others in the Arsenal side who ought to have asked more of a League Two defense. And yet when chasing a game for 70 minutes, is it fair to ask for more than three-quarters of an xG from the senior attacker of the English champions, a man who has scored in two Champions League finals?Wanting a bit more has been a familiar experience for both Chelsea and Arsenal during his time with them. For the Gunners, it has been over two and a half years since they discovered just how good Havertz could be for them. The shift to center forward in a 3-1 win over Sunday's opponents, Liverpool, was the start of a brilliant year leading the line. Across 37 Premier League games, the Germany international delivered 18 goals and nine assists, not Erling Haaland numbers but exceptional output for the center forward in Arteta's everyone-eats offense.
Even since that brilliant run, there have been flashes. For an hour in May's Champions League final, Havertz was as threatening an attacker as anyone in PSG colors. A few weeks earlier he had been excellent in defeat to Manchester City, not the first time he had bossed Arsenal's title rival. If Chelsea have the misfortune of running into their former star, they're probably going to get him in the mood to do some damage. Of all the attackers available to Arteta this week, Havertz is the nearest he has to a big-game hunter.  Indeed, if you want to make the case against Arsenal "just signing a striker" in January (you shouldn't), a key component of your argument ought to be how few players suit this manager as well as a fully fit Havertz. It is just that, well, a fully fit Havertz has been an elusive creature.  And yet if Arteta will not use injuries as justification for the current wobble, perhaps we shouldn't. And wobble this is. Through eight league games, Havertz is averaging fewer shots, goals and non-penalty xG than in any other season in his Arsenal career on a per-90 basis. The same is true when you adjust for the fact that the 27-year-old is touching the ball a bit less on average this season than last.  There is one notable stat where Havertz's numbers have skyrocketed, though, and that is in offsides. In every Premier League season before this one, he was caught out behind the opposition defense on less than one occasion per 90 minutes. In most of them, he averaged around one offside per two full games played. This year, however, no one in the league matches Havertz's 10 offsides already, and the gap is not particularly close. Joint-second on seven are his teammate Bukayo Saka and Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds.Passes made by Arsenal this season that resulted in their players being caught offside 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Now, the sample size of minutes is still small and open to distortion. It might be that one explanation for Havertz's skyrocketing offsides is that he has played Aston Villa and their occasionally effective, invariably cavalier high line. Equally, not all of those 10 offsides are about what the defense did well or about a run that came at just the wrong moment from the center forward. Watch Havertz move a good moment too soon to collect a pass off his friend and captain Martin Odegaard before bending well wide from a promising shooting position against Villa, and you see what looks like a forward who is simply off color, nothing more and nothing less, really. Sometimes the easiest explanation is the correct one. Havertz is just a bit out of sync with both his game and that of his teammates, as his manager acknowledged on Friday."That kind of form and that kind of efficiency with the front players, it's very common," said Arteta. "Full trust on him and what he's doing."
The natural response, then, for Arteta would be to pick the next cab off the rank, as he did in the win over Everton where Viktor Gyokeres started. That was the Swede's best game of the season, but he still did not register a shot. Gyokeres scored against Fleetwood but took only two other shots. Per 90, he averages 0.92 shots, 16th on Arsenal, with both left backs ahead of him. The evidence of his past entanglements with elite opposition suggests that Gyokeres is not the player to turn to at Anfield.Instead, it will be Havertz, in need of something of a jump-start to his season. While he retains the "full trust" of a manager who has never faltered in his support, there might be time enough to sniff out his best form. Viewing information -- Liverpool vs. ArsenalDate: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 11:30 a.m. ETLocation: Anfield, Liverpool, United KingdomTV: USA | Live stream: fuboTVOdds: Liverpool +188; Draw +230; Arsenal +138

title: Canelo Alvarez with a point to prove in title fight with Christian Mbilli - CBS Sports
description: Alvarez takes on a hungry Christian Mbilli on Saturday with a point to prove to fans, pundits and himself
body:
Alvarez takes on a hungry Christian Mbilli on Saturday with a point to prove to fans, pundits and himself
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the exception of the ongoing political tensions in the region, the biggest question facing Saturday's super middleweight title bout in Saudi Arabia is quite simple. How much does 36-year-old Mexican superstar Canelo Alvarez have left after 68 fights and 21 years as a professional?Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) will snap a 13-month layoff following elbow surgery when he challenges Christian Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) inside Kingdom Arena in Riyadh (1 p.m. ET, DAZN PPV) for the WBC title that Alvarez lost via unanimous decision in his last appearance against Terence Crawford in 2025. For the record, Alvarez is listed as high as a 3-to-1 betting favorite against the hard-charging Mbilli, a 31-year-old native of Cameroon who fights out of Montreal. But given Mbilli's conditioning and aggressive style, along with the concern as to how hungry Alvarez still is, especially after the humbling nature of seeing Crawford, two weeks shy of his 38th birthday, move up effectively three weight divisions to defeat him in their superfight. 

        
            
                Who is Christian Mbilli? Get to know the WBC super middleweight champ ahead of Canelo Alvarez showdown
                
                    Brent Brookhouse                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
On the pre-fight "Face Off" show produced last month by DAZN, Alvarez and Mbilli answered questions while seated across the table from one another. Alvarez was asked directly whether he has any doubt in the back of his mind that he has lost a step from the multiple peaks of his prime, which includes titles in four weight divisions, a three-year stretch as the sport's pound-for-pound king and a 2021 run to the undisputed championship at super middleweight.With a cold, emotionless look on his face, Alvarez quietly responded by saying, "No, I'm very good." 
In fact, the only time Alvarez showed emotion of any kind was when Mbilli, in a respectful but matter-of-fact tone, shared his belief that his opponent was old.
"Yes, [Alvarez] is old now, but he is still very dangerous," Mbilli said. "He has very good power, a good counter punch [but] I think it's the best timing for me to have this fight. I think maybe his power has gone down just a little bit. I think five years ago, he was at a different level, but now he's a little bit down, I think."The response brought out a sinister smile from Alvarez, who could only laugh. "He's going to find out," Alvarez said. "Not even if I am 50 years old, he can't beat me. It's just different levels. He's going to find out that this level is way different. "You need like 10 of you to beat me."If we're inspecting it with a microscope, Alvarez's decline in recent years has been very gradual. But if it's possible to find a marker in the sand when he effectively peaked for the final time, it would be 2022. 
Alvarez entered that year fresh off the most active stretch of his elite run, where he recorded four victories in an 11-month stretch, including three wins over unbeaten champions at 168 pounds and three of them by stoppage. Whether it was sensational wins over Callum Smith, Billy Joe Saunders or Caleb Plant, Alvarez was operating at the top of his game and could seemingly do whatever he wanted, from walking down his foes to countering from the outside or choosing to outslick them technically. But in May of 2022, the daring-to-be-great nature that defined Alvarez's career effectively found its ceiling when he moved back up to light heavyweight and was physically handled in a close yet convincing decision loss to unbeaten champion Dmitry Bivol, marking Alvarez's first loss in nine years.Even though Alvarez won his next two fights over the next year in decisions over Gennadiy Golovkin (in their trilogy bout) and John Ryder, he looked noticeably flat and had to fight off late rallies from both. But talk around the sport that Alvarez had noticeably lost a step was explained away by the fact that he pushed through both training camps with a wrist injury in order to delay surgery that left him unable to push as hard in preparation. 
Yes, following surgery, Alvarez went on to win his next four fights over the next two years leading up to the Crawford bout. But, all four fights went to the scorecards – further extending Alvarez's knockout draught – and all four opponents appeared either overwhelmed (Jermell Charlo, William Scull) by the moment and unwilling to engage or simply not on the same skill level (Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga). Alvarez then entered the Crawford fight as the betting favorite with perceived advantages in everything from age and size to power, but was ultimately outworked and outthought at every turn in a competitive decision loss that elevated Crawford on his way into retirement to the pantheon of the all-time greats, along with the title of being the best of his era. In reality, the loss didn't change much for Alvarez historically. Not only has he been the singular face of the sport for more than a decade, but he's arguably the greatest boxer in Mexico's legendary history. Yes, he lost a trio of his biggest fights against fellow all-time greats in Floyd Mayweather, Bivol and Crawford but he also owns wins over Miguel Cotto, Sergey Kovalev (at light heavyweight), Erislandy Lara and twice defeated Golovkin in their highly disputed rivalry. 
The biggest thing the Crawford loss did was make Alvarez's legion of fans come to the reality that he's no longer the same guy, whether Alvarez himself wants to believe it or not. "When you lose, you always look back at your mistakes, and at this level, there's very little between a win and a loss," Alvarez said during the final week of his training camp in Spain. "I did a good job of preparing for the [Crawford] fight, but throughout fight week, my mind wasn't there. I always say, I don't want to look back on things. Now, I'm going to learn from that [fight] and look towards Mbilli. I think his style is perfect for me to go against and will make for a great fight." From an entertainment standpoint, it's hard to disagree with Alvarez about Mbilli. Regardless of the result, the fight will be all-action and largely contested on the inside, not just because an aging Alvarez is no longer willing to chase (see the 2025 Scull fight) as he once did against Lara and Austin Trout, but because Mbilli only knows one way: forward. 
Last September, on the Crawford-Alvarez undercard, Mbilli endured the lone blemish on his resume in a non-stop brawl against unbeaten Lester Martinez that was lauded as one of the best fights of the year. Mbilli left any thoughts of defense in the locker room and fought at a hellacious pace for all 10 rounds but was unable to break the equally durable Martinez in a fight that was ruled a split draw and left Alvarez less than impressed. "They throw punches like crazy and, of course, that is good," Alvarez said. "But it's not boxing."If Alvarez is still even 70% of who he was in 2021, he should handle Mbilli by disciplining him with his accurate, crushing counter shots, with the possibility of scoring his first knockout since the Plant fight not out of the question. But if he's not, Mbilli is the wrong opponent at the wrong time with good power, a swarming style, tons of confidence and a hunger to make his name known on a global level. 
Who wins Alvarez vs. Mbilli, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $2,500 on his combat sports picks last year, and find out.

title: Demarcus Henry commits to UNC: Five-star wing gives Michael Malone massive recruiting win - CBS Sports

body:
The No. 4-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting class by 247Sports is the son of late NFL wide receiver Chris Henry
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Dan Fritz | 247Sports
            
            

    
        Five-star forward Demarcus Henry committed to North Carolina on Friday, giving first-year coach Michael Malone his first major recruiting win on the high school trail. Henry, the No. 4 overall player and the top-ranked small forward in the 2027 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, is UNC's first commitment in the upcoming class.Henry is the son of late NFL wide receiver Chris Henry, who died in 2009. Henry's older brother, Chris Henry Jr., was a five-star wide receiver prospect in the 2026 class and is currently a freshman at Ohio State. The Compass Prep (Chandler, Arizona) product committed to North Carolina over Louisville, Arkansas and Kentucky. Henry took an official visit to North Carolina last weekend after previously visiting those three schools and UConn.247Sports Director of Scouting Adam Finkelstein says Henry's defensive upside is worth keeping an eye on.
Between his size, length, and movement skills, his defensive upside is extreme. He projects as being very switchable and already possesses impressive playmaking numbers with over 3 stocks per game in the EYBL (1.8 steals and 1.3 blocks). He's also an excellent wing rebounder who pulled down 9.2 (including 2.9 on the offensive end) in the EYBL and 8.4 in EYBL Scholastic play.Notably, Henry is the highest-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting class to announce his pledge. Beckham Black, CJ Rosser and Cayden Daughtry — the top-three ranked players in the upcoming recruiting cycle — remain uncommitted. This week, however, was busy on the high school front with several blue-chip players announcing their respective commitments. Henry was joined by Lewis Uvwo (Providence), Reese Alston (LSU) and Asa Montgomery (Duke) as players from the class who committed this week.

While the neutral venue has changed, the intensity will be the same when No. 3 Georgia meets No. 17 Florida

        No. 3 Georgia and No. 17 Florida will be squaring off somewhere other than Jacksonville for the first time since 1995 on Saturday, as the historic rivals take the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party indoors at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Saturday. With Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium under renovation until August 2028, the setting will be different.The stakes remain the same. In fact, there may be an even higher degree of intensity to this year's showdown between the border foes because of the circumstances. It's the first time since 2020 that both are ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC) is coming off a bye week after a stunning home loss to Auburn, and Florida (5-2, 3-2) is riding high off an Oct. 17 road win over Texas. First-year Gators coach Jon Sumrall already has two wins over top-10 teams (Ole Miss and Texas) and could get his team firmly in the College Football Playoff hunt with another marquee win.The Bulldogs have won five straight meetings in the series, but Sumrall has reinvigorated the Florida program this season since arriving from Tulane. The Gators have shown the ability to slay some of the SEC's top dogs already this season, and Georgia will need to be on high alert to avoid suffering consecutive regular season losses for the first time since Kirby Smart's first season in 2015.
  Georgia vs. Florida: Need to know  Florida's quarterback situation: Starting in place of the injured Aaron Philo, Florida sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. rose to the occasion in a Week 7 win at Texas. The inexperienced quarterback completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions against the Longhorns' vaunted defense while also totaling 41 rushing yards. But will he play against Georgia? Philo was listed as questionable on the Gators' first student-athlete availability report this week, raising questions over who will get the nod under center. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he doesn't plan to name a starter before the game, which will force Georgia to prepare for both QBs. Jones is more mobile, but he's also put his full repertoire on tape now. Philo is still dealing with a right shoulder injury, but he did practice this week.Georgia's run defense: Regardless of who starts at quarterback for Florida, the Gators are going to try and lean on their run game. Georgia's run defense has shown some vulnerability in the past two games. Led by quarterback Byrum Brown, Auburn totaled 192 yards rushing against the Bulldogs in an Oct. 17 upset road win over UGA. The week before, Alabama amassed 161 yards on the ground against Georgia. Up until those two games, Georgia's run defense had been stout. Facing Florida might be the toughest test yet of Georgia's ability to stop the run. The Gators raced to a 4-0 start, including wins over Auburn and Ole Miss, by rushing for 200+ yards in each game. The UF rushing game has been less effective in three games since then, but star back Jadan Baugh is a load to handle. He leads the SEC in rushing touchdowns with 13 and is third in rushing yards with 763.CFP implications: Georgia's chances of reaching the College Football Playoff will rise to 94.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. Those odds would dip to 72.7% with a loss. Entering Saturday, Florida has just a 9.5% chance to make it, but that mark would surge to 29% with an upset win over the Bulldogs. On the flip side, suffering a third loss would leave UF with just a 5.6% chance of making the playoff. If the Gators suffer a third loss against Georgia, they would need to run the table against Oklahoma, Kentucky, Vanderbilt and Florida State and then get some help from other teams to have any shot at reaching the field with a 9-3 record.

Florida will have the Bulldogs' full attention after an upset win at Texas, and UGA won't be remotely caught off guard by anything the Gators attempt offensively. Georgia's defensive staff knows Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner well. On the opposite side, the Gators have shown they are vulnerable on defense, and Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton will be playing with a chip on his shoulder after a rare poor performance against Auburn. Pick: Georgia -12.5

body:
Noah Fifita leads the surging Wildcats into Lubbock against a reeling Red Raiders squad trying to stay in the Big 12 title race after an upset loss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No. 13 Texas Tech hosts No. 22 Arizona in a pivotal Big 12 battle in the desert. The Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 stunner against Cincinnati in which they allowed 255 yards on the ground. Texas Tech started consecutive seasons 6-0 for the first time in program history, but now face a critical bounce-back spot to stay in the Big 12 title race. Since losing to BYU in Week 2, the Wildcats have taken off. Arizona has won five straight games, including three straight in Big 12 play by an average of 28.0 points per game. Last week, the Wildcats bottled up Iowa State in a 39-3 performance behind 300 yards from quarterback Noah Fifita. Arizona and Texas Tech have played 34 times, with the Red Raiders holding a dominant 27-5-2 advantage, but only two have come since 1989. In their only meeting as Big 12 opponents, the Red Raiders outlasted the Wildcats 28-22 as Fifita threw for 300 yards, but served up two interceptions.   Texas Tech vs. Arizona: Need to know  Inconsistent play: Despite the 6-1 start, Texas Tech has struggled to find consistency on either side of the ball. The Red Raiders rank in the bottom half of both total offense and defense in the Big 12 as neither unit has strung together consistent performances. For comparison, Texas Tech ranked top two in the Big 12 in both categories last season. Fifita's growth: The Arizona quarterback is setting career highs in every category during a sensational senior season for the Wildcats. Fifita leads the Big 12 with a 74% completion rate and a 174 passer rating, and ranks top 10 nationally in passing at just a shade under 295 yards per game. Since losing to BYU, Fifita has thrown for 275 yards and two touchdowns in every game during the five-game winning streak. 
Quarterback questions: Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond was only thrust into starting duty after losing starter Brendan Sorsby to a gambling scandal. The Austin native has struggled, throwing six touchdowns to six interceptions and only completing one pass of more than 15 yards against Cincinnati through the first three quarters. Texas Tech could get a bigger dose of backup Tommy Castellanos against the Wildcats if Hammond can't work the offense. Where to watch Texas Tech vs. Arizona live  Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 12 p.m. ET  Location: Galaxy Stadium -- Lubbock, Texas  TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Texas Tech vs. Arizona prediction, picks  Arizona might be the most underrated team in the country, and Noah Fifita is playing the best ball of his career. Cincinnati exposed major holes in Texas Tech's defense during an upset win, and the Wildcats are even better positioned to take advantage. Unless the Red Raiders offense can find something, Arizona will waltz away with a marquee victory. Pick: Arizona +3.5

title: Nick Saban advises Texas, Steve Sarkisian to use 'the bench' to motivate Arch Manning - CBS Sports
description: Saban had no problem benching high-profile players in big spots during his legendary coaching career
body:
Saban had no problem benching high-profile players in big spots during his legendary coaching career
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arch Manning's inconsistency has plagued the Texas offense this season, and a recent threat from Steve Sarkisian potentially prompted the former five-star quarterback to play with more poise last time out, according to Nick Saban.Saban was no stranger to benching players in his time at Alabama. He famously sat Jalen Hurts in favor of Tua Tagovailoa at halftime of the Tide's 2018 national title game against Georgia, prompting a memorable comeback win. "I always say the bench is a pretty good motivator, especially if the guy's a great competitor, which I think Arch is," Saban said Friday on ESPN. "The threat that he might not be entitled to the job may be something that motivates him and keeps him motivated through the rest of the season. He's going to have to play well for them to be able (to win out)."Backup KJ Lacey has played sparingly this season despite a recent reported uptick in first-team reps during practice, and hasn't faced the complexity of live SEC rounds like Tagovailoa.In both of the Longhorns' losses this season, Manning made critical fourth-quarter mistakes that swung the game's momentum, and he did it against Ole Miss too with the game tied, but Texas escaped.
"Sark made it very clear when he had a meeting with Arch and said to him, 'Look, we can't win with this guy,'" Saban said. "It's always a tough decision for a coach to make a change like that when you have a high-profile player who's very capable and has shown at times he's very capable. But at the same time, I think if Arch doesn't continue to play with consistency, Sark's going to keep it in the bag."What Texas faces nextAfter Saturday's game against Mississippi State, the No. 11 ranked Longhorns (5-2) embark on a season-defining November stretch that includes trips to ranked Missouri and LSU before Arkansas and Texas A&M round out the campaign.Texas is currently slotted as an at-large selection in our updated College Football Playoff projections entering the weekend and ahead of Tuesday night's first CFP top 25 reveal from the selection committee.
Winning out all but guarantees a spot in the CFP and could get Texas to another SEC Championship appearance. Going 4-1 over their final five games means the Longhorns likely find themselves in a logjam of nine-win SEC teams. Then it comes down to overall resume and whatever the selection committee chooses to deem important during the final process.
